notes: The front hall is the hinge of the house: the main stairs rise from it to the stair head, and the dining room and library open off it, while the back stair runs from the stair foot below stairs up to the study end of the gallery, so staff can reach the study door without crossing the front of the house. Below stairs, the stair foot serves the servants' hall, the housekeeper's room and the serving pantry, and the yard door of the servants' hall gives onto the drifted yard that must be crossed to reach the ice house.

connective.name: the drifted yard
connective.description: The kitchen yard lies under two days of snow, trodden to a single grey channel between the servants' door and the ice house mound. The pump is frozen to its handle and the coal store door has drifted shut. Wind comes over the stable roof and lifts the loose snow into the face, so that the house behind seems to retreat into white. Somebody has been out here since the last fall: there is a second line of prints, half filled, that does not go to the ice house at all.

frame.composition: Wide shot at eye level from the servants' door, looking across the yard to a low brick mound
subjects: Trodden channel of grey snow between drifts
Frozen iron pump with icicled spout
Half-filled line of footprints veering toward the stable wall
frame.environment: Flat snow light under a lead sky, brick walls rimed white, wind-blown powder in the air
frame.palette_mood: Grey-white, soot black, cold brick red; bleak, exposed, watchful
frame.prompt_summary: Graphic novel plate, Victorian kitchen yard buried in snow, single trodden path to a brick ice house, frozen pump, stray footprints, grey storm light

examinable.name: the second line of prints
examinable.description: A man's boot, by the size, going out toward the stable wall and coming back, filled to half their depth. The snow stopped at four this morning; they were made before that.

examinable.name: the pump
examinable.description: Frozen solid, the handle furred with ice. Nobody has drawn water here since the storm began; the kitchen has been melting snow.

adjacent.label: up the main stairs
adjacent.text: The oak treads take your weight without a sound, the banister cold under your glove as the grey light thins above.
adjacent.back_text: You descend with one hand on the rail, the hall's draught rising to meet you at each step.

adjacent.label: through to the dining room
adjacent.text: The double doors part on a breath of cold air and the smell of yesterday's candles.
adjacent.back_text: You draw the doors to behind you and the hall's flagstones ring faintly underfoot.

adjacent.label: into the library
adjacent.text: The library door sticks in its swollen frame and then gives all at once.
adjacent.back_text: The door drags shut behind you and the hall clock resumes its measured tick.

adjacent.label: through the broken study door
adjacent.text: You step over the splintered jamb where the lock was forced, the door hanging askew on one hinge.
adjacent.back_text: You edge back past the hanging door, careful not to set it swinging.

adjacent.label: up through the baize door
adjacent.text: The baize door sighs on its spring and lets you out of the dark onto the carpeted hush.
adjacent.back_text: The baize door closes on the gallery and the stairwell's cold rises to meet you.

adjacent.label: into the servants' hall
adjacent.text: You push through the low door into the warmth and the smell of damp wool drying.
adjacent.back_text: The door swings to behind you and the passage draught finds your ankles at once.

adjacent.label: to your own room
adjacent.text: Your key turns in the familiar lock and the door opens on your own small quiet.
adjacent.back_text: You lock the door behind you from habit and step back into the passage.

adjacent.label: down the service passage
adjacent.text: The passage slopes underfoot, flagstones sweating cold, until the candle box shows at the bottom.
adjacent.back_text: You climb the sloping passage, the smell of silver polish growing with each step.

adjacent.label: out by the yard door
adjacent.back_label: back in by the yard door
adjacent.text: The yard door needs a shoulder against the drift and the wind takes your breath on the step.
adjacent.back_text: You stamp the snow from your boots on the sill and haul the door shut against the wind.

adjacent.label: across to the ice house
adjacent.text: You follow the trodden channel through knee-deep snow to the low brick arch, the cold deepening with every step.
adjacent.back_text: You come up out of the cold into the open wind, snow sifting into the path behind you.
